title: Pattanam excavation find record (candidate site of ancient Muziris)
language_note: English-language excavation reporting by the Kerala Council for Historical Research (KCHR); no single regional-language primary text — included as an archaeological/artefact anchor (Pillar 4).
date: Mediterranean-linked layers: 100 BCE - 400 CE; site occupation from c. 1000 BCE
findspot: Pattanam, near North Paravur, Ernakulam district, Kerala, India; excavated 2007-2014 by KCHR
original_text_excerpt: Mediterranean objects (100 BC to 400 AD): Amphora and terra sigillata shards; fragments of Roman glass pillar bowls; and gaming counters. West Asian, South Arabian, and Mesopotamian objects (300 BC to 1000 AD): turquoise glazed pottery; torpedo jar fragments; frankincense crumbs. Most remarkable: a fired brick wharf complex with nine teak bollards and a mummified 6-metre dugout canoe (Artocarpus hirsutus).
original_text_note: Summary drawn from Wikipedia's synthesis of KCHR season reports; pull the primary KCHR 'Pattanam Seventh Season Handbook' (linked in citation_original) for the authoritative excavation-report text during ingestion.
notes: Physical corroboration for the textual Muziris cluster (southasia-01 through -03): Roman amphora/terra sigillata shards and a 1983 hoard of Roman coins found ~9.7 km inland support the port identification. DNA analysis of skeletal remains also shows West Eurasian genetic imprints, though ASI has urged caution pending further sampling — worth flagging as a contested/uncertain claim in the eval harness rather than an established fact.
